title: CapabilitySet.summary() in src/lua/capabilities.zig does not compile under Zig 0.16 (stale std.ArrayList(u8).init) — a public, uncalled function body that `zig build test-lua` reports as green
symptom:
`src/lua/capabilities.zig:49` reads `var buf = std.ArrayList(u8).init(allocator);` inside `pub fn summary()`. `std.ArrayList(T)` has no `init` in Zig 0.16 (the type is unmanaged; the spelling is `std.ArrayList(u8).empty`, with the allocator passed to each append/deinit call). This is a hard compile error, yet `zig build test-lua` reports 71/71 tests passed and `zig build test` is green.

Verified empirically, not inferred: adding a throwaway test rooted under src/ that calls `caps.summary(std.testing.allocator)` turns the target red with
    src\lua\capabilities.zig:49:36: error: struct 'array_list.Aligned(u8,null)' has no member named 'init'
Removing that call restores green. The function's body is never analysed by any existing build path.

`summary()` additionally has an unfixed API mismatch beneath the compile error: the doc comment and the ISS-0169 design (§4.2) describe `summary()` as the renderer of the 'granted:' field in a capability-denial message, and `docs`/design reference `CapabilitySet.summary()` as rendering `"(none)"` for an empty set. Its `.deinit()` call on line 50 also uses the pre-0.16 no-allocator form, so migrating line 49 alone is not sufficient.
root_cause: The ISS-0172 / GH #500 blind spot again, now in a third subsystem (after src/lua/instruction_limiter.zig + memory_limiter.zig in ISS-0172, and src/oidc/jwks.zig in ISS-0173). `src/lua_test_root.zig` pins this file with `_ = lua.capabilities.CapabilitySet;` — a bare TYPE reference. Zig resolves struct field types lazily and does not semantically analyse a `pub fn` body that no reachable code calls. `CapabilitySet.summary` has ZERO callers in the repository: `src/lua/host_context.zig` deliberately does NOT call it (ISS-0169 design §4.4 / invariant ERR-2 — it allocates, and its result would be leaked across `lua_error`'s longjmp, so `writeGrants` renders the grant set into a fixed stack buffer instead). Removing the last caller is precisely what made the stale API call invisible.
acceptance_criteria: src/lua/capabilities.zig compiles under Zig 0.16 with its function bodies genuinely analysed: `std.ArrayList(u8).init(allocator)` migrated to the unmanaged 0.16 API (`.empty` plus allocator-passing `appendSlice`/`toOwnedSlice`/`deinit`).
A build target CALLS `CapabilitySet.summary()` and asserts on its output — for an empty set (`"(none)"`) and for a multi-grant set (comma-separated) — rather than pinning the type (see ISS-0172).
Deliberate-mutation verification: inject a statement error into `summary`'s body and confirm `zig build test-lua` goes red.

A decision is recorded on whether `summary()` should exist at all: ISS-0169 removed its only intended caller by design (ERR-2). If it is dead code it should be deleted rather than repaired, since an uncalled allocating helper on a security type is a liability. If it is retained for host-side (non-longjmp) callers, that contract is documented on the function.

The census recommended by ISS-0173 is extended to cover public functions with zero callers, not only modules with zero callers — this instance is a function-level blind spot inside a file that IS otherwise reachable.
notes: Filed and forwarded per CLAUDE.md 'Unblock-Everything' scope boundary and docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md. It does NOT block ISS-0169 tranche 1: nothing on the capability-enforcement path calls `summary()` (that is a deliberate design decision, ERR-2), and `zig build`, `zig build test` and `zig build test-lua` are all green on the WF03-ISS-0169-20260806 branch (71/71).

Discovered while writing the LUA-05/06/07 capability-enforcement tests: the same `std.ArrayList(u8).init` spelling was written into the new test file, the compiler rejected it there, and grepping the fix target surfaced the identical stale call surviving in capabilities.zig — where no compiler had ever looked.

Security-relevant in the same sense as ISS-0173: `capabilities.zig` is the authorization type for the Lua host API. A public method on it that has never been compiled cannot be assumed correct, and a future caller adding it back would hit a compile error attributed to their own change.

This is the THIRD instance of the ISS-0172 pattern found in two consecutive runs (ISS-0172, ISS-0173, ISS-0174). The recurrence rate is itself evidence that the type-pin idiom in the *_test_root.zig files is systematically unsafe and should be replaced repo-wide, not patched per-file.

Reproduce: append to src/lua_test_root.zig a test calling `var c = lua.capabilities.CapabilitySet.init(std.testing.allocator); defer c.deinit(); try c.add("variable:read"); const s = try c.summary(std.testing.allocator); defer std.testing.allocator.free(s);` and run `zig build test-lua`.
